ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Lou Gehrig Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient with progressive weakness and loss of coordination: evaluation for a motor neuron disorder and its mimics, safety, and how he wants to receive results. Concerns: Over about a year he has lost strength and coordination, fumbles with buttons and a bat, trips on curbs, and fell on the ice in the winter, and he wants to know why; He has stopped playing and wants plain answers, delivered to him first; He wants to stay useful and to keep working in some form. [S]

list.item: Progressive weakness and loss of coordination for about a year: fumbling with buttons and a bat, tripping on curbs, a fall on the ice in the winter, muscle cramps and twitching in the arms and thighs; no numbness, pain, double vision, or trouble speaking or swallowing. Examination: wasting of the hand muscles (left more than right), fasciculations in both arms and thighs, weakness of grip and of left ankle dorsiflexion, brisk reflexes with spread and a positive Hoffmann sign, normal sensation. Mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs; evaluation for motor neuron disease and its mimics begun, with neuromuscular neurology consultation booked: resolved, confirmed [S]

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, limb onset: progressive weakness for about a year with upper and lower motor neuron signs in the cervical and lumbosacral regions, and active and chronic denervation on EMG in the cervical, thoracic and lumbosacral regions with normal sensory nerve conduction; MRI of the brain and cervical spine and blood tests exclude mimics. Meets the Gold Coast criteria and the revised El Escorial category of clinically probable ALS. ALSFRS-R 42 and FVC 88% of predicted at diagnosis. Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented diagnosis: active, confirmed [S]

Sprain of the left lateral ankle ligaments after tripping on a curb with left foot drop, while not wearing his ankle-foot orthosis: swelling and tenderness over the anterior talofibular ligament, able to bear weight, no bony tenderness by the Ottawa ankle rules; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: New patient with progressive weakness and loss of coordination: evaluation for a motor neuron disorder and its mimics, safety, and how he wants to receive results
Neuromuscular neurology consultation with EMG and nerve conduction studies; results of MRI and blood tests; diagnosis and start of treatment
Six weeks after diagnosis: riluzole safety, genetic test result, multidisciplinary ALS clinic, mobility, mood, and his decision about work
Three months after diagnosis: ALSFRS-R, breathing, weight, speech, mobility equipment, and work accommodations
Five months after diagnosis: breathing tests and noninvasive ventilation planning, nutrition and gastrostomy discussion, and his new desk work
Same-day sick visit for a left ankle sprain

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Evaluation of progressive weakness with mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs: blood count, metabolic panel with calcium, creatine kinase, vitamin B12, TSH, A1c, serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation, and an HIV test; MRI of the brain and cervical spine; seated spirometry
Neuromuscular neurology consultation with EMG and nerve conduction studies for progressive weakness with mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs

Safety while the evaluation proceeds: no competitive play or heavy lifting, a physical therapy assessment of balance and gait, home fall precautions (night lights, rails, no loose rugs), and a same-day call for any trouble swallowing or breathing; results given to him first, in person

Riluzole 50 mg twice daily, with ALT monthly for the first 3 months and then every 3 months, and a blood count with any fever; genetic testing with genetic counseling for ALS-associated genes, with tofersen only if an SOD1 variant is found; edaravone discussed as an option with modest evidence in a selected group

Multidisciplinary ALS clinic every 2 to 3 months (neurology, nursing, physical, occupational and speech therapy, nutrition, respiratory therapy, social work and mental health): ALSFRS-R, seated forced vital capacity and maximal inspiratory pressure, and weight at every visit; cognitive and behavioral screening; PHQ-9

Respiratory plan: forced vital capacity and maximal inspiratory pressure every visit, supine capacity and overnight oximetry when values fall or symptoms appear; noninvasive ventilation when forced vital capacity is below 50% of predicted, maximal inspiratory pressure is weaker than -60 cmH2O, overnight oximetry shows desaturation, or orthopnea or morning headaches appear; influenza and COVID-19 vaccines

Nutrition, speech, swallowing and mobility: a high-calorie diet to keep weight stable, with gastrostomy discussed early, while forced vital capacity is above 50%; speech and swallowing assessments every visit and voice banking; a left ankle-foot orthosis, a cane, and an early power wheelchair evaluation because of lead times; home and car adaptations

Work and planning: workplace accommodations for a desk role (accessible office, flexible hours, rest breaks, voice-recognition software, parking), information on disability benefits, social work support, and early advance care planning, revisited at each change
A clear diagnosis, with mimics excluded, within four weeks
Diagnosis made at two weeks on EMG, MRI and blood tests
No falls, using an ankle-foot orthosis, a cane, and a safer home
One fall with an ankle sprain in July, on a day the orthosis was not worn; no falls since it has been worn for all walking outdoors
Weight held within 5% of the weight at diagnosis
89.2 kg at diagnosis and 86.6 kg at five months (2.9% lower)
Breathing tracked every visit, with noninvasive ventilation started as soon as criteria are met
FVC 72% and no symptoms at five months; overnight oximetry ordered
Goals of care, a health care agent, and his wishes about ventilation and feeding recorded early and revisited
Agent named and wishes recorded at the preventive visit
Working in a role that suits him, with accommodations
Started a desk role in public service with accommodations
